key_insight: The paper proposes steering neural network training with interpretable partial-dependence constraints so model behavior matches prior functional knowledge.
engineering_relevance: This enables more data-efficient regression models whose learned relationships are both predictive and aligned with domain expectations, which is valuable in engineering systems modeling and forecasting.
method: Use partial dependence to express desired average input-output behavior.
Add constraints during training so the network’s response follows user-provided functional knowledge.
Apply the approach to regression tasks, including dynamical systems forecasting.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports empirical tests across multiple regression problems, showing constrained models outperform unconstrained ones and need less data, while their interpretations better match the provided knowledge.
watch_item: The method depends on having accurate prior functional knowledge and correctly specified partial-dependence constraints, which may be difficult to define in practice.
paper_title: Steering Neural Network Training through Interpretable Constraints Based on Partial Dependence
